set.body:
Goal: add LDA as a NEW method built on secondOrder — the proof that the pullback generalizes, on new code, before any further shipping method is touched. Design: docs/plans/multivar-operator-core.md §10 (Phase 2).

LDA is currently absent from multivar (no Lda type). Between- and within-class scatter are literally the same primitive with different row links:
- Sʙ = Xˢ · Lʙ · X  and  Sᴡ = Xˢ · Lᴡ · X, where Lʙ/Lᴡ are class-incidence row links constructed from a ClassDesign via RowRelationships (Lʙ = A·P_B, Lᴡ = A·P_W).
- Fisher LDA: objective GeneralizedRayleigh(Sʙ, S̃ᴡ) normalized by the within-scatter operator. Trace-ratio LDA: TraceRatio(Sʙ, Sᴡ) with a separate geometric normalization.
- Within-class scatter shrinkage is an OperatorPolicy (S̃ᴡ = (1−α)Sᴡ + ατQ), a statistical-estimate change UPSTREAM — NOT a ridge on discriminant weights (§6.5, law 20).

Acceptance: `Lda.problem(x, classes, within, k)` returns a typed OperatorProblem; the fit returns a FunctionalFrame plus discriminant scores; a NEW R parity fixture against a reference (e.g. MASS::lda) with an explicit tol; flows secondOrder → compress → linalg solver (no new engine); JVM+JS green. If this proves clean, the pullback abstraction is validated for Phases 3–4.
set.title: Multivar: add LDA via secondOrder (between/within scatter) — proof the pullback generalizes
